paper_claims.claim: Stocks of firms classified as low-B/M by Fama-French methods significantly accelerate capital investment prior to the classification year (Panel A Table I).
Average monthly returns are significantly lower for high-investment-growth firms than for low-investment-growth firms (Table II).
Investment growth is a significant cross-sectional predictor of stock returns and subsumes part of the information in B/M (Table III).

Within investment-growth portfolios, evidence of a value premium is weakened; returns on small-vs-big and high-vs-low B/M stocks are statistically indistinguishable for high investment-growth firms (Table IV).

An investment-based factor (INV) explains returns on investment-sorted portfolios as well as or better than the FF three-factor model; INV correlates with returns across B/M-sorted and MVE-sorted portfolios (Table V).

budget_flag: Tables III and V contain 26 and 13 cells; Table I adds 50 cells (25 size*B/M means + 25 medians); plus Table III subperiods (M5) and the Ln(inv) scale diagnostic (M2). Total committed ~110 cells, under the 350-cell soft cap.

tables.description: Mean and median of prior 2-year investment growth for 5x5 size x B/M portfolios (1976-1999). NYSE breakpoints, positive B/M only, top/bottom 1% of inv_growth trimmed.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that investment growth is decreasing in B/M (across rows) and decreasing in size (across columns). Tests the universe construction (5x5 NYSE breakpoints on size and B/M, positive B/M only, 1%/99% trim of inv_growth) and is the cheapest test of the [M2] Compustat-vintage hypothesis (paper's range of means 0.17-1.03 and medians -0.05-0.54).
tables.paper_quote: Table I presents preliminary evidence on the associations among investment, MVE, and B/M. Panel A displays mean and median values of two-year investment growth rates for 25 portfolios sorted by MVE and B/M following Fama and French (1993).
tables.notes: 5x5 size x B/M portfolios. Each cell reports the time-series mean of per-year mean (or median) of inv_growth across firms assigned to that cell. NYSE-only breakpoints on size (me_jun_form) and B/M (bm). All firms with positive B/M included in cell assignment. Top and bottom 1% of inv_growth observations clipped (inv_growth in (-0.99, 10)). Paper's range: means 0.17-1.03, medians -0.05-0.54. 50 metrics (25 cells x 2 stats). Each cell is scored against the paper's value; tolerance_pct is wide because the cell range is dominated by the 1%/99% winsorization band.

tables.description: Equal-weighted average monthly returns for 10 decile portfolios sorted on prior 2-year capital-investment growth (1976-1999)
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the core empirical claim that prior investment growth predicts lower returns, including the cross-sectional spread across deciles and the supporting standard deviations. Tests universe (NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ common stocks, non-financials), the FF-style annual rebalancing at end of June, decile sorting by INV, and equal-weighted portfolio returns.
tables.paper_quote: Table II shows that investment growth over the prior two-year period, our proxy for the exercise of growth options, is consistently associated with lower B/M and lower realized returns. The table reports monthly averages of equally weighted raw returns for ten portfolios based on growth rates in capital expenditures from fiscal year t-3 to t-1.
tables.notes: Equal-weighted monthly returns; 10 deciles ranked in descending order so decile 1 = highest investment growth (lowest realized returns) per paper convention. All numbers are monthly percent (decimal * 100). Spread metric computed as decile1 - decile10.

tables.table_ref: Table III (Panel A, full sample only)
tables.description: Fama-MacBeth monthly cross-sectional regressions of stock returns on size, B/M, beta, and investment growth (1976-1999, N=276 months)
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the paper's headline claim that investment growth is a robust negative predictor of returns and subsumes part of B/M. Tests Fama-MacBeth procedure (per-month cross-sectional regressions averaged into time-series t-stats); the 1%/99% winsorization; the natural-log transforms of MVE, B/M, and INV; and the joint MVE+B/M+INV specification. The most quantitatively demanding table in the paper.
tables.paper_quote: Table III contains the results of Fama and MacBeth (1973) regressions where parameter estimates are time-series averages of the cross-sectional slopes of monthly returns regressed on size, B/M and growth rates in capital expenditures. ... When recent corporate investment growth is included in the regressions, its parameter estimate is highly significant and has the expected negative sign. The regression of stock returns on investment growth produces an estimate of -4.19%, with a t-statistic of -6.00.
tables.notes: Reported coefficients are in percent units and represent the time-series averages of monthly cross-sectional OLS slopes. T-statistics are means over time-series standard errors of the slopes. Numbers scaled from decimal-return units in our pipeline to percent in the table by multiplying by 100. The INV coefficient sign (negative) is the headline claim. Models 1 and 7 (require beta) are now evaluated (joined via data/fm_panel_with_beta.parquet).

tables.description: Regressions of monthly excess returns on investment-growth quintile portfolios (1976-1999) against MKT, SMB, HML, and INV (the paper's investment-growth factor)
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that an INV factor (high-minus-low investment growth) explains the cross-section of returns on investment-sorted portfolios. Tests factor construction: low-minus-high (or per FF convention, equal-weighted high-minus-low) investment-growth quintiles each June, held for 12 months; construction of INV factor returns; and time-series regression of portfolio excess returns on MKT, SMB, HML, INV. Subsumes Sub-claim C5.
tables.paper_quote: We next subtract the returns on the high investment group from the low investment group each month, starting in July. In this manner we construct a portfolio-based factor comparable to the HML and SMB factors constructed by Fama and French.
tables.notes: Five investment-growth quintile portfolios with value-weighted returns; INV factor = low-minus-high (panel A row 'Highest' = highest inv growth, lowest expected returns). All coefficients are decimal-return units (the paper's Table V prints percent with no explicit unit; treat '0.006' as 0.6%/month, i.e., the coefficient is reported in pct). The 4-factor specification is the closest test of the paper's hypothesis that INV subsumes SMB and HML for explaining investment-sorted returns. Two weightings are reported: (a) contemporaneous me_dollars (original shipped weighting, biased by [M1]) and (b) lagged me_lag (corrected). The committed metrics in this file use the LAGGED-weight results; the contemporaneous-weight results are also reported in the table_5.md artifact.
